# Area summaries {#sec-areas}

Linking the tabular synthesis outputs from @sec-synthesis with the polygon areas of TASVEG 5.0 allows us to quantify the statewide extent of each IUCN GET Ecosystem Functional Group—and to evaluate how sensitive area estimates are to (1) **membership weighting** (unweighted total polygon area vs. membership-weighted area) and (2) **aggregation choices** (individual interpreters vs. multi-interpreter consensus, and all candidates vs. best-candidate only).

:::{.aside}

Our setup for this R session loads spatial (`sf`, `units`; @Pebesma_2018), cross-referencing (`ecoSynthesis`), and tidyverse/plotting packages, along with the saved lookup and synthesis tables:

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
library(sf)
library(ecoSynthesis)
library(dplyr)
library(units)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
```

```{r}
here::i_am("synthesis/area-summaries.qmd")
output_dir <- here::here("../results/XREFs")
source(here::here("../scripts/setup.R"))
load(here::here(output_dir, "lookup-tables.rda"))
load(here::here(output_dir, "memb-summaries.rda"))
```

:::

## Computing polygon areas from TASVEG 5.0

We read the TASVEG 5.0 statewide polygon shapefile using `sf::read_sf()`, select the classification fields (`VEG_GROUP`, `VEGCODE`, `VEGCODE_D`), calculate each polygon's area via `sf::st_area()`, and immediately drop the geometry column (`sf::st_drop_geometry()`) so all subsequent joins and summaries execute quickly on a lightweight attribute table:

```{r}
TASVEG_xy <- read_sf(here::here("..", "gisdata", "LIST_TASVEG_50_STATEWIDE", "TASVEG_5_0.shp")) |>
    select(VEG_GROUP, VEGCODE, VEGCODE_D)

TASVEG_areas <- TASVEG_xy |>
    mutate(area = st_area(geometry)) |>
    st_drop_geometry()
```

## Individual-interpreter weighted area estimates

In cross-referencing area calculations, each TASVEG `VEGCODE` occurs across many map polygons, and each `VEGCODE` may carry fuzzy membership to multiple target EFGs. This workflow assumes that the source-to-target membership vector applies uniformly across all polygons belonging to the same `VEGCODE`.

First, we perform a `many-to-many` left join between `TASVEG_areas` and the individual Round 2 assessments (`TASVEG_revised`), coding non-eligible polygons (`OAQ`, `OSM`, `ORO`) explicitly as `"!XREF"`:

```{r}
EFG_memb_exp_areas <- TASVEG_areas |> # nolint: object_name_linter.
    left_join(TASVEG_revised, by = "VEGCODE", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
    mutate(EFG = coalesce(EFG, "!XREF"))
```

To incorporate cross-referencing uncertainty into extent estimates, we compare:

- **Unweighted total area** ($\sum \text{area}$): full extent of every polygon with positive membership to the target EFG.
- **Membership-weighted area** ($\sum \text{area} \times \text{memb}$): scales each polygon's contribution by its fuzzy membership proportion.

Using **`T2.5` (*Temperate pyric humid forests*)** as a concrete example, we summarise unweighted and weighted areas (in $\text{km}^2$) by interpreter and whether `T2.5` is the best candidate (`best = TRUE`) or a secondary candidate (`best = FALSE`):

```{r}
EFG_memb_exp_areas |>
    filter(EFG == "T2.5") |>
    summarise(
        nr_VEGCODE = n_distinct(VEGCODE),
        mean_memb = mean(memb),
        area_total = set_units(sum(area), "km2"),
        area_weighted = set_units(sum(area * memb), "km2"),
        .by = c(expert, EFG, best)
    ) |>
    filter(!is.na(area_total))
```

Because interpreters assign slightly different sets of secondary communities and fuzzy weights to `T2.5`, both the unweighted and weighted area estimates vary across interpreters.

To inspect which individual TASVEG units drive that difference, we aggregate polygon areas to `km²` per `(expert, VEGCODE)`, split each unit's total area into `assigned_area` ($\text{area} \times \text{memb}$) and `remaining_area` ($\text{area} \times (1 - \text{memb})$), and reshape long for stacked bar plotting:

```{r}
plot_data <- EFG_memb_exp_areas |>
    filter(EFG == "T2.5") |>
    summarise(
        total_area = sum(drop_units(set_units(area, "km2"))),
        .by = all_of(c("expert", "VEGCODE", "memb", "best"))
    ) |>
    mutate(
        sid = reorder(VEGCODE, total_area),
        assigned_area = total_area * memb,
        remaining_area = total_area - assigned_area
    ) |>
    pivot_longer(
        cols = c(assigned_area, remaining_area),
        names_to = "segment",
        values_to = "height"
    ) |>
    mutate(segment = factor(segment, levels = c("remaining_area", "assigned_area"))) |>
    arrange(sid)
```

Plotting all units assigned positive membership to `T2.5` faceted by interpreter reveals that several spatially extensive TASVEG communities carry only low secondary membership weights—contributing substantially to *unweighted* area totals while adding only modestly to *weighted* area estimates:

```{r}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 7
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = sid, y = height, fill = segment)) +
    geom_col(position = "stack") +
    scale_fill_manual(
        values = c("assigned_area" = "#db349e", "remaining_area" = "#e1a6cb"),
        labels = c("assigned_area" = "Assigned (area * memb)", "remaining_area" = "Remaining area")
    ) +
    labs(
        title = "TASVEG units assigned to T2.5 by interpreter (all candidates)",
        x = "Source units ordered by total area",
        y = "Area (km²)",
        fill = "Component"
    ) +
    facet_wrap(~expert) +
    theme_wp3() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 6))
```

Restricting the same chart to units where `T2.5` is the **best candidate** (`best == TRUE`) removes those low-weight secondary communities and highlights the high-consensus core communities of `T2.5`:

```{r}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 7
ggplot(filter(plot_data, best), aes(x = sid, y = height, fill = segment)) +
    geom_col(position = "stack") +
    scale_fill_manual(
        values = c("assigned_area" = "#db349e", "remaining_area" = "#e1a6cb"),
        labels = c("assigned_area" = "Assigned (area * memb)", "remaining_area" = "Remaining area")
    ) +
    labs(
        title = "TASVEG units assigned to T2.5 by interpreter (best candidate only)",
        x = "Source units ordered by total area",
        y = "Area (km²)",
        fill = "Component"
    ) +
    facet_wrap(~expert) +
    theme_wp3() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 7))
```

## Aggregated multi-interpreter area estimates

Next, we repeat the spatial join using `TASVEG_summary` (aggregated Round 2 `prop_memb` across all five interpreters from @sec-synthesis) so every polygon is linked to the consensus membership proportions:

```{r}
EFG_memb_agg_areas <- TASVEG_areas |>
    left_join(TASVEG_summary, by = "VEGCODE", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
    mutate(EFG = coalesce(EFG, "!XREF"))
```

Summarising `T2.5` from the aggregated table splits total and `prop_memb`-weighted areas cleanly between primary (`best == TRUE`) and secondary (`best == FALSE`) source communities:

```{r}
EFG_memb_agg_areas |>
    filter(EFG == "T2.5") |>
    summarise(
        nr_VEGCODE = n_distinct(VEGCODE),
        mean_memb = mean(prop_memb),
        area_total = set_units(sum(area), "km2"),
        area_weighted = set_units(sum(area * prop_memb), "km2"),
        .by = c(EFG, best)
    ) |>
    filter(!is.na(area_total))
```

Reshaping the aggregated `T2.5` table into `assigned_area` ($\text{area} \times \text{prop\_memb}$) and `remaining_area` lets us compare primary vs. secondary contributing communities side by side:

```{r}
plot_data_agg <- EFG_memb_agg_areas |>
    filter(EFG == "T2.5") |>
    summarise(
        total_area = sum(drop_units(set_units(area, "km2"))),
        .by = all_of(c("VEGCODE", "prop_memb", "best"))
    ) |>
    mutate(
        sid = reorder(VEGCODE, total_area),
        assigned_area = total_area * prop_memb,
        remaining_area = total_area - assigned_area
    ) |>
    pivot_longer(
        cols = c(assigned_area, remaining_area),
        names_to = "segment",
        values_to = "height"
    ) |>
    mutate(segment = factor(segment, levels = c("remaining_area", "assigned_area"))) |>
    arrange(sid)
```

Faceting the stacked bars by `best` (`FALSE` = secondary candidate, `TRUE` = primary/best candidate) visually contrasts how secondary units contribute minor fractional slices while primary units carry high consensus membership:

```{r}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 7
ggplot(plot_data_agg, aes(x = sid, y = height, fill = segment)) +
    geom_col(position = "stack") +
    scale_fill_manual(
        values = c("assigned_area" = "#db349e", "remaining_area" = "#e1a6cb"),
        labels = c("assigned_area" = "Assigned (area * prop_memb)", "remaining_area" = "Remaining area")
    ) +
    labs(
        title = "Aggregated TASVEG units assigned to T2.5 (secondary vs. best candidate)",
        x = "Source units ordered by total area",
        y = "Area (km²)",
        fill = "Component"
    ) +
    facet_grid(best ~ ., labeller = label_both) +
    theme_wp3() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 6.5))
```

## Statewide comparison across all IUCN GET functional groups

Finally, we compute weighted area estimates across **all** candidate EFGs for both individual interpreters (`d1`, hollow circles) and the aggregated consensus (`d2`, filled circles), keeping primary (`best == TRUE`) and secondary (`best == FALSE`) contributions distinct:

```{r}
d1 <- EFG_memb_exp_areas |>
    summarise(
        nr_VEGCODE = n_distinct(VEGCODE),
        mean_memb = mean(memb),
        area_total = set_units(sum(area), "km2"),
        area_weighted = set_units(sum(area * memb), "km2"),
        .by = c(expert, EFG, best)
    ) |>
    filter(!is.na(area_total))

d2 <- EFG_memb_agg_areas |>
    summarise(
        nr_VEGCODE = n_distinct(VEGCODE),
        mean_memb = mean(prop_memb),
        area_total = set_units(sum(area), "km2"),
        area_weighted = set_units(sum(area * prop_memb), "km2"),
        .by = c(EFG, best)
    ) |>
    filter(!is.na(area_total))

plot_data_all <- bind_rows(d1, d2)
```

Plotting membership-weighted area on a $\log_{10}$ scale across all EFGs shows (1) how tightly individual interpreter extent estimates cluster around the aggregated consensus for dominant terrestrial EFGs, and (2) which EFGs exist purely as secondary components (`best = FALSE`, e.g. minor wetland or freshwater functional groups) versus dominant mapped ecosystems (`best = TRUE`):

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 9
ggplot(plot_data_all) +
    geom_point(
        aes(
            y = EFG,
            x = drop_units(area_weighted),
            shape = is.na(expert),
            colour = best
        ),
        size = 3.5,
        alpha = 0.85
    ) +
    scale_x_log10() +
    scale_colour_manual(
        values = c("FALSE" = "peru", "TRUE" = "orchid4"),
        na.value = "grey50",
        name = "Is best candidate?"
    ) +
    scale_shape_manual(
        values = c("TRUE" = 19, "FALSE" = 21),
        labels = c("TRUE" = "Aggregated consensus", "FALSE" = "Individual interpreter"),
        name = "Estimate type"
    ) +
    labs(
        title = "Statewide membership-weighted area across all candidate EFGs",
        x = "Membership-weighted area (km², log10 scale)",
        y = "IUCN GET Ecosystem Functional Group (EFG)"
    ) +
    theme_wp3()
```
